priceSnapshot.note: The breakout was tested overnight and it held. Endday published at 86,266.8; twelve hours and fifty-three minutes later spot is 85,985.0, down 281.8 points or 0.33 percent on the handover and up 1.14 percent on the 24-hour open of 85,013.0. The path between the two reports is the whole story. Price slid for seven hours into a 05:00 UTC low of 85,111.1 - 214.1 points BELOW endday's 85,325.2 reduce gate and, more importantly, 520.2 points below the 85,631.3 January shelf the breakout is built on - and the 04:00 UTC four-hour bar actually settled back under that shelf at 85,344.9. Then the 08:00 UTC hour reversed the whole thing with a single 870.6-point bar, closing 86,215.5, and the 08:00 UTC four-hour body settled at 85,992.6, back above the shelf. Not one settled 1H close printed below 85,325.2 - the lowest was 85,344.9, a margin of 19.7 points - so the gate endday wrote survived by less than twenty dollars.

reduceIf.confirmation: A settled 1H close below 85,325.2 - the same gate endday wrote, deliberately left where it is. It was tested overnight by a wick to 85,111.1 and defended by 19.7 points on a settled-close basis, which is exactly the test that earns a level the right to stay. Moving it down to the 85,111.1 wick low would be fitting the gate to noise; moving it up would throw away a line the market just validated. A wick underneath is still not enough, and that rule is now 3-for-3 this week: 82,099.0 on 19 and 20 September, and 85,325.2 last night.

addIf.confirmation: This is the CONTINUATION add, because the retest add already filled. A settled 1H close above 86,632.6 - the high of the 00:00 UTC hour and the last swing high before the overnight slide - would say the reclaim has turned into trend and would leave only 86,899.8 and the 87,399.0 eight-month high overhead. The lower add, a pullback into the 85,750.0 to 85,600.0 shelf that holds on a settled 1H close, remains live as a second tranche: 85,750.0 absorbed 756,135 USD of long liquidations in the last four hours and has been defended twice, at 85,680.9 and 85,584.3.

decisionBox.changed: Position moves from endday's TAKE_PROFIT back to ADD, and it is a pre-committed rule firing rather than a change of mind. Endday trimmed 10 percent of the spot book at 86,266.8 and named the conditions that would buy it back: a retest that HOLDS. The retest came, it was uglier than advertised - 85,111.1 is 488.9 points below the 85,600.0 endday nominated - and it held where it had to, on settled 1H closes above 85,325.2. Spot is now 85,985.0, which is 281.8 points cheaper than the trim. Four facts support pressing rather than waiting. FIRST, the momentum reset is the cleanest thing on the chart: 4H RSI has come down from 86.43 to 75.18, an 11.25-point unwind, while price fell only 0.33 percent - the oscillator extreme endday banked against has been worked off by time, not by damage. SECOND, Farside has REVISED 21 September up from the 617.6 million USD endday read to 999.0 million, making it the largest single-day US spot-ETF inflow of the month by a wide margin and the three-day streak worth 1,591.5 million rather than 1,210.1. THIRD, Brent is 98.48, down 1.85 percent on the day and back under 100 for the first time this week, with the 10-year easing to 4.947 percent - the macro backdrop got friendlier overnight, not hostile. FOURTH, funding settled at 0.0001, the practical floor, and the OKX long/short account ratio is 1.01: nobody is paying to be long and the crowd is flat, so there is no leverage overhang to unwind. Against that, 1H MACD histogram is negative at minus 143.29 and 15m at minus 19.01, which is why this is a retest add and not a chase - the reduce gate stays at 85,325.2, invalidation stays at 84,719.5, and the resting stop stays at 84,650.0.

liquidation.note: 756,135 USD of LONG liquidations against 275 USD of shorts across 25 fills, by far the largest cluster in the window and 235.0 points below spot. This is where the overnight slide actually killed leverage. Realized fills map where leverage has already died, not where stops rest now - which cuts both ways: the weak longs at this shelf are gone, and the level has since been defended twice at 85,680.9 and 85,584.3.

112,847 USD of long liquidations and zero shorts across 43 fills - the most individual fills of any bucket, which is the signature of a grind rather than a flush. It sits between the defended 85,584.3 low and the 85,325.2 reduce gate, so it is the first real air pocket underneath.

50,684 USD of SHORT liquidations against 9 USD of longs across 13 fills - the only meaningful short-side pocket on the map, 265.0 points above spot and just under the 86,406.3 session high. Clearing it is what a continuation attempt has to do first.

24,472 USD of short liquidations and 868 USD of longs across 19 fills, essentially on top of live spot at 85,985.0. A thin bucket; it says the round number is being traded through rather than defended.

liquidityMagnet.note: Realized fills over the last three hours and thirty-nine minutes ran 869,859 USD of longs against 75,431 USD of shorts, an 11.5-to-1 long flush - but almost all of it happened INTO the 85,750.0 shelf on the way down, and price has since recovered above it. That is why the pull is called balanced rather than down: the crowded side has already been paid out. Confirming it, the OKX long/short account ratio is 1.01 and has printed 1.00, 1.01, 1.00, 1.01, 1.00, 1.01 over the last six hourly buckets - dead flat, up from 0.93 at endday, so accounts covered shorts into the reclaim rather than piling into longs. Open interest is 2,623,474,386 USD, UP 2.31 percent from endday's 2,564,275,351 while price is down 0.33 percent: positions were rebuilt on the dip, which adds fuel in both directions and is the main reason the 85,750.0 to 86,250.0 box is where a whipsaw would live.

calibration.rollingRecord: Morning sessions before this run: the weakest of the four slots at plus 7.20 USDT attributed, against endday plus 41.47, midnight plus 21.03 and midday plus 11.45. Wallet round 1, status active, zero bankruptcies. Net worth was 216.87 USDT at the 86,266.8 endday mark against a 227.80 endowment.
calibration.note: Endday was right twice and the row records both. The READ: reduce gate at 85,325.2 on a settled 1H close, and the lowest settled 1H close overnight was 85,344.9 - clearance of 19.7 points, the tightest margin any gate has survived this month, while the wick went 214.1 points through it to 85,111.1. priorReduceFired is false, and the specific sentence endday wrote - a wick underneath is not enough - is now 3-for-3 this week. The TRADE: endday sold 10 percent of the spot book at 86,266.8 and spot is 85,985.0, so the trim is 281.8 points or 0.33 percent onside, worth roughly plus 0.06 USDT, and actingHelped is true. The honest caveat is that the sizing, not the direction, is what made it work: a 10 percent trim on a 0.33 percent move is worth almost nothing either way, and the real value was keeping 90 percent long through a night that dipped 1,155.7 points. The standing error to keep naming is still the 21 September morning trim at 84,742.7, which is 1,242.3 points offside at this mark - better than the 1,524.1 it was last night, but the lesson has not been paid back yet. This morning applies its correction directly: the retest arrived, it held on settled closes, and this session buys rather than waits for a prettier level.
